raw_response:
I farm a small piece of land, only 4.1 mu, so I count every bag and every watering. I do not like changing too much. I start from what worked before and what I see in the next fields. For wheat, I will keep the field in the usual wheat-maize turn, put most of the fertilizer in before or at sowing, then add nitrogen again when the wheat stands up in spring. Wheat in our place is the crop I do not dare starve, so I will keep fertilizer a little on the safe side. With well water, I will plan on 2 irrigations for wheat in a normal year. If spring turns very dry, I will add one more, but for the yearly plan I will count 2. For maize, I will sow soon after wheat harvest, use the hybrid seed people nearby use when it shows a full ear and steady yield, and I will give enough fertilizer at sowing plus one chase later. Summer rain usually helps maize, so I will count 1 irrigation, and only use more if the rain fails. On such a small farm, I will not spend on fancy things, but I will not save money by letting the crop go hungry either. I would rather waste a little fertilizer than lose grain.
